extracted.intended_audience: aspiring comic-book writers; fans of Alan Moore; anyone interested in the craft of writing comics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and craft principles for writing comics/graphic novels, covering medium-specific thinking, reader engagement, worldbuilding, plotting, and scripting. Based on Alan Moore's essays on comic-book authorship and technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: The basic idea: thinking about comics
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic idea : thinking about comics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the medium-specific nature of comics — how comics communicate and how that should inform the writer's approach. (Chapter heading from the book; implies guidance on conceptualizing stories specifically for comics rather than other media.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reaching the reader: structure, pacing, story telling
rubrics_metrics.description: Reaching the reader : structure, pacing, story telling
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes how to structure a comic, manage pacing across panels/pages, and craft storytelling that effectively engages and guides the reader. (Original wording lists these as the key subtopics for reaching the reader.)

rubrics_metrics.name: World building: place and personality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a sense of place and give the setting personality; build the world so it supports character and story in ways unique to the visual-comic medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: The details: plot and script
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attention to plotting and the mechanics of scripting — concrete techniques for turning story ideas into comic scripts, including scene construction, beats, and dialogue suited to sequential art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Afterwords
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postscript/reflective material (the book includes afterwords, including a later essay on how Moore's thoughts changed), suggesting reflection on craft over time and revision of earlier views; no specific prescriptive detail on the page.
